_comment: Atlas Weekly Review realistic trial investor profile. Anonymized placeholder data. Not investment advice.
name: Long-Term Quality Investor
investment_goals: Preservation of purchasing power over a 7-10 year horizon
portfolio_purpose: Core long-term portfolio — quality compounders and evidence-based research
principles: Evidence before opinion: no position status change without documented evidence review
Avoid forced position changes: thesis change must be distinguished from price movement
Concentration discipline: review is required when any position exceeds 20% of portfolio
Cash is a position: reserve capacity is intentional and should not be deployed without evidence
Long-term horizon: capital allocation decisions should reflect 7-10 year expected holding periods
Quality over cyclicality: prefer businesses with recurring revenue and durable competitive positions
No action warranted is a valid review outcome: avoid action bias
constraints: Avoid concentrated exposure above 25% in any single position
Avoid speculative or early-stage companies without meaningful revenue history
Maintain minimum 3% cash reserve at all times
Avoid decisions based on recent price movement without accompanying evidence review
Avoid adding complexity without a clear evidence-based reason
notes: Long-term portfolio with quality focus. Evidence discipline and patience are more important than reaction speed. No action is often the correct outcome.
